question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}4xy,\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y<2X-2{X}^{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
If $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability density function for the random variables $X$ and $Y$ and $A⊂{R}^{2},$ then

$$
P((X,Y)\in A)={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonnegative in the region $D=[0,1]\times [0,1],$ and the event $A=\{Y<2X-2{X}^{2}\}$ corresponds to a subset of $D,$ shown as the shaded region below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14270355/assets/bb3b94fbd5ae245b60fbd496be1a4609742bb1958148faeae57ca3ef4054f6da.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<2X-2{X}^{2}) & ={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x-2{x}^{2}}4xy\,\text{d}y\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2x-2{x}^{2}}4xy\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[2x{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=2x-2{x}^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2x(2x-2{x}^{2})^{2}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(8{x}^{3}-16{x}^{4}+8{x}^{5})\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{4}-\frac{16{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{4{x}^{6}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2-\frac{16}{5}+\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
